decision: started stage 2 on top of the committed design note
why: user said to implement the note's decisions on drop-tla2tools-pin and commit as we go

decision: removed Amp orbs and exec before anything else, then moved the CLI and host to apps/
why: decision 9 and 10; less code to carry through the redesign

decision: rewrote MachineAnswers.tla as row plus operation with control plane crash, host restart, partition, lost, repeated and late delivery
why: the brief asks for those failures in the interleavings, and the old model's actors are gone

decision: stopped the 2-client all-faults run at 152M distinct states with no violation, unfinished
why: its queue was still growing after 40 minutes, so it can't be the check anyone reruns

decision: bounded lost deliveries with MaxDrops like every other fault
why: liveness failed on Send then Lose forever, which is an unfair network, not a protocol bug

decision: split the check in two: one client with every fault and liveness, two clients with crash and partition only
why: the full cross-product doesn't finish; these two do

decision: dropped generation from the public Machine and from the client's wait
why: break-test: removing the client's check changed nothing, as store.desire leaves rest in the same write, so a resting phase already means the request was seen

decision: plain per-machine loop instead of xstate, lifecycle.ts deleted
why: a loop over row and operation is all the statechart still did once steps run on the host
result: deviation from note, to record there

decision: phase and prepared are persisted on the row
why: a control plane restart must not re-prepare a machine or lose what a client is waiting on

decision: leases are derived from the operations table, taken in one transaction
why: in-memory leases can't survive a restart now that the steps outlive the process

decision: make is copy plus setup, and preparation stays in start
why: a failed preparation keeps the machine while a failed setup deletes it, so one step can't hold both; narrows decision 2's wording
result: deviation from note, to record there

decision: admission stays on the host inside the operation, with the machine list from the control plane
why: only the runtime can read what is really running at the moment it boots; note said control plane
result: deviation from note, to record there

decision: port picked by the host at accept and reported back
why: only the host can probe a port is free; delete and observe take name and instance alone
result: Tart finds its forwarder by name

decision: pin comparisons all on the host, steps carry the pin
why: the host is what knows its own pin; the control plane only stores it

decision: a wait fails fast with Unavailable when a row rests at waiting, instead of timing out
why: a client hanging on an unreachable host helps nobody and the request is saved anyway; note said timeout
result: deviation from note, to record there

decision: the server never returns Superseded, the client works it out from the row
why: the server answers at once now, so only the wait can know

decision: Unavailable became a server-sent error with status 503, only ever a synchronous refusal, never on a row
why: create needs to say no host answered; it must not read as a failed step

decision: a failed delete retries at the recheck, tracked by a flag in the loop
why: the draft spun on a failing delete

decision: store.begin refuses when the row's generation moved
why: a step decided from a stale read must not start

decision: finish of an undone patch deletes the row when a delete arrived meanwhile
why: otherwise the row stays undone with desired deleted and a client waits forever

decision: added fences: server domain files, hosts.ts as the one caller of a host, Store adapter, server composition never loads the host package, host contract stays schemas, host adapters can't import node:sqlite
why: the brief asks for rules on the new boundary, and a client reaching a host must fail lint

decision: apps/server/tests/serve.ts serves the control plane over hosts served by apps/host/tests/serve.ts in separate processes
why: a kill must take one process and leave the other, so they can't share one

decision: generation check removed from the model; a desire break and an answer-before-rest break added
why: every invariant needs a break that fails it; the first desire break tripped FailedSays only because it cleared the error
evidence: desire break keeping phase and error: RestTrue; answer before rest: AnswerTrue; TwoClients 11,466,662 distinct and MachineAnswers 9,608,391 distinct, both No error, exit 0

decision: a host gone for good stays unknown; a forget action is unbuilt
why: the brief does not ask for one and a real forget needs a product call on what happens to its rows
evidence: docs/design/control-plane.md section 4; no action in packages/sdk/src/api.ts

decision: fence settings proven by forbidden imports, no new rule file
why: the boundary is settings of fence/allowed-imports, whose logic tools/lint-fence already tests
evidence: nine probes each reported fence(allowed-imports): CLI to host contract, server to host package from domain and composition, host adapter node:sqlite, a server domain file calling a host, host domain to composition, host contract to Node, server adapter to Node, provider to host contract

decision: every SDK client method fails with ClankerboxError instead of a narrow union per method
why: narrow per-method types needed a cast through located(); callers match by tag, so the width costs little
evidence: SDK delegate report; packages/sdk tsc clean; 150 tests

decision: client reply timeout 15 s, above the server's 10 s and the host read's 9 s
why: at 10 s a silent host could fail a client before the server named it

decision: the model keeps one create; a delete's wait over a recreated name is covered by client tests only
why: recreation is outside the model's stated bound, and adding it grows the state space for a case the wait answers with no row logic

decision: the server's listen.address takes the host's rule, shared from the SDK's ./node
why: the control plane can change every machine with no auth, so it must never listen where a guest or the internet reaches it; the delegate left it open

decision: a checkpoint drive that ends re-runs when a request arrived during its exit
why: the state delegate reported a delete landing as drive exits would wait until the next restart
evidence: inferred from checkpoints.ts; no deterministic test, the window is one fiber yield

decision: host port exhaustion is a failed report, not a defect
why: a defect reads as unreachable and retries the same host; a Capacity report moves the create
evidence: operations.test.ts; removal of a VM never made is safe on smolvm (returns on missing) and Tart (exit 2 allowed)

decision: no lock against two host processes on one state dir, left out
why: the old lock left with the store; a shared listen port already refuses the same config twice

decision: the model refuses a non-delete request on an undoing row, as asked does
why: the code answers NotFound there, and a model broader than the code describes something else
evidence: TwoClients 11,175,654 distinct, MachineAnswers 9,034,147 distinct with AllAnswered, No error, exit 0

decision: a make reported cancelled with no delete asked is undone
why: running it again would run on a half-made VM with its script possibly gone

decision: fault run: control plane killed mid-create
why: the brief's done-means names this end state
evidence: built CLI, scratch HOME: slow create --no-wait, setup-began, KILL, Unavailable while down, setup-go, restart; get says settled, recipe-ran slow-recipe; runtime-calls one create, one setup exec, one start

decision: fault run: host killed, and a create past a full host
why: adding a host must add capacity with the client seeing nothing
evidence: 2G creates landed one per host; third answered Capacity and rested failed; kill-host: phase waiting, stop answered Unavailable saved, create landed on the survivor

decision: verify flows from a scratch HOME on linux and mac, and packed programs
why: the brief's done-means
evidence: every row of features/README.md driven; three tarballs installed, --version matches, --config in help, no config exits 1

decision: store property tests get a 30 s timeout
why: one failed in a full run under TLC load; each takes 1.6 s alone against 5 s and CI has fewer cores
evidence: 805 passed on three later runs; the failing run's message was not captured, so a timeout is inferred

decision: setup scripts leave no trace in the store or logs
why: the house style says never stored or logged
evidence: canary in a profile recipe: 0 hits across server-state files and all logs; the control read found it in the profile

decision: the checkpoint drive clears its marker once, in the repeat's check
why: advisor review: the marker was cleared twice, so a drive starting between lost it and every later request forked another

decision: packages/host-contract stays unpublished
why: npm publishes every non-private package
evidence: private true; pnpm ls lists five public packages, not the contract

decision: an operation carries boot and another host process refuses it
why: cross-model review: the model's Deliver drops a stale boot but the host did not check one, so the model claimed a fence the code lacked

decision: a restart ends a Capacity move
why: the hosts left to try live in memory with the setup; persisting them moves nothing, since a scripted make can't be resent
evidence: machines.ts movedPastCapacity needs creates.get; recorded in the note

decision: start and stop steps carry the control plane's last seen state
why: the host's resumable decision keys on it and a host keeps no row

decision: ephemeral builders are asked deleted at every restart
why: their prebuild's state is in memory, so nothing can finish them

decision: adoptMachines once per new boot, through a boots table
why: a host keeps no list, and a runtime may need the machines to reattach
evidence: crash.test.ts a host that restarts is told the machines it holds, once

decision: rows 19 to 21 and the to-record rows closed
why: cross-model review found no closing row

decision: trail rows 2 to 23 were written in one batch after the work
why: they were not logged at decision time; timestamps do not show when each was decided

decision: a wait reads on through waiting as through an outage, ending Unavailable after outageLimit
why: one failed host read ended a create's wait, and the provider then deleted a healthy create
evidence: packages/sdk/src/client.ts; client.test.ts, a machine whose host can't be read

decision: execMachine is a pass-through request, not an operation
why: a command leaves nothing to resume after a restart, and a row or log line of it would hold what its stdin carries; the control plane waits for a step in flight and the host for one in its scope, so a step never runs under a command
evidence: apps/server/src/machines.ts exec; apps/host/src/operations.ts exec; machines.test.ts exec waits for a step in flight

decision: labels are set at make time only, and lists filter by them
why: an immutable label is a fact about the make, so no write races another over it, and a copy takes only its own request's labels
evidence: packages/sdk/src/resources.ts Labels; machines.test.ts labels go on a machine at its make

decision: a pause with a capture records the capture first, waits for its operation to begin, then records the pause with after; the capture's share lease holds the pause
why: no new wake plumbing: the lease conflict already orders them, and a read that finds the capture unbegun holds the pause until the next recheck
evidence: apps/server/src/checkpoints.ts pausing; machine-chart.ts awaiting; checkpoints.test.ts a pause with a capture across a restart

decision: a ready checkpoint past expiresAt is deleted by a sweep at each recheck, through the ordinary delete
why: one path deletes checkpoints, so a failed delete runs again as any does; a prebuild never carries an expiry
evidence: apps/server/src/checkpoints.ts sweep; checkpoints.test.ts a ready checkpoint past its expiry

decision: the SDK's ensure is a client helper over the contract, not an action
why: start-or-restore-or-create is a client's policy, and the server keeps one request per write

decision: Amp orbs are a package beside the control plane, a dispatch program over the client contract, with the orb's and the snapshot's IDs on labels
why: the control plane stays free of any one caller's model, and 0.35's ensure, pause with capture, expiry, labels and exec cover every job
evidence: packages/amp-orbs/src/dispatch.ts; dispatch.test.ts; a live spawn, pause with snapshot, respawn and delete against the home control plane

decision: a build keeps the base, sizes and setup timeout it was built from, and a template's are its current build's, or its newest's while none is ready
why: a copy is checked against the base its build named, so a rebuild onto another base left every copy of the older build outdated, and a create pinned to it NotBuilt
evidence: apps/server/src/templates.ts currentOrNewest; templates.test.ts a rebuild onto another base; sqlite.test.ts a state dir that 0.37 wrote

decision: a wait on a machine always holds its reads, with no polling fallback for a control plane that names no version
why: no server that answers a 0.36 client takes no hold: 0.35 refuses another release, and 0.36 names its version, so the fallback served only the SDK's stub
evidence: packages/sdk/src/client.ts machineRead; stub-server.ts getMachine holds a read that finds no change
